guide.title: A week in Kansas City
guide.author: Nate Bird
guide.summary: Seven days of barbecue and jazz, fountains and boulevards, the WWI museum and the Nelson-Atkins, with a Chiefs or Royals game if you can.

places.name: Hotel Kansas City
places.notes: A 1923 Tudor-style gentlemen's club turned hotel, with a dark, cozy bar downstairs.

places.name: The Raphael Hotel
places.notes: A small 1927 hotel across from the Plaza, with fountains and shopping out the door.

places.name: 21c Museum Hotel Kansas City
places.notes: A hotel with a free contemporary art museum inside, in the old Savoy building.

places.name: Crossroads Hotel
places.notes: A converted 1911 brick warehouse in the arts district, with a rooftop bar and a restaurant downstairs.

places.name: Joe's Kansas City Bar-B-Que
places.notes: Barbecue in a working gas station. Order the Z-Man sandwich, and expect a line out the door.

places.name: Arthur Bryant's Barbeque
places.notes: The burnt ends and sauce that made Kansas City barbecue famous. Close to the jazz district.

places.name: Gates Bar-B-Q
places.notes: Hear the counter staff shout "Hi, may I help you?" as you walk in. Get the ribs.

places.name: Q39
places.notes: Competition-style barbecue with a sit-down room. The burnt end burger is a favorite.

places.name: Jack Stack Barbecue
places.notes: The Freight House location, with a long bar and crown prime beef ribs. Book for dinner.

places.name: LC's Bar-B-Q
places.notes: A smoky little room with a pit you can see from the door. Burnt ends on white bread.

places.name: Corvino Supper Club
places.notes: Japanese-influenced plates with live jazz in the supper club, or the tasting room for a splurge.

places.name: Bluestem
places.notes: A long-running fine-dining spot in Westport. The lounge has a shorter menu for walk-ins.

places.name: The Rieger
places.notes: Pork soup and seasonal cooking in a 1915 hotel bar. The Manhattan Club is downstairs.

places.name: Town Topic Hamburgers
places.notes: A tiny 24-hour burger counter since 1937. Sliders, fries and a malt.

places.name: City Market
places.notes: A farmers market since 1857, with year-round shops and restaurants. Best on a Saturday morning.

places.name: Messenger Coffee
places.notes: A three-story roastery and bakery with a rooftop. A good start to a Crossroads day.

places.name: Christopher Elbow Chocolates
places.notes: Jewel-like chocolates and an excellent drinking chocolate.

places.name: Betty Rae's Ice Cream
places.notes: Small-batch ice cream with a line on summer nights. Try a scoop of whatever's new.

places.name: Tom's Town Distilling Co.
places.notes: An Art Deco distillery named for the city's Prohibition boss. Gin cocktails and tours.

places.name: Green Lady Lounge
places.notes: Live jazz every night, no cover, in a dark red room.

places.name: Boulevard Brewing Co.
places.notes: Kansas City's brewery. Take the tour and finish at the rooftop tasting room.

places.name: National WWI Museum and Memorial
places.notes: The country's museum of the Great War, and outstanding. Ride up the tower for the skyline view.

places.name: Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
places.notes: A free, world-class museum. Find the giant shuttlecocks on the lawn.

places.name: Kemper Museum of Contemporary Art
places.notes: A free contemporary art museum next to the Nelson-Atkins, with a giant spider out front.

places.name: American Jazz Museum
places.notes: Charlie Parker, Count Basie and the Kansas City sound. The Blue Room jazz club is next door.

places.name: Negro Leagues Baseball Museum
places.notes: The story of Black baseball, ending on a field of bronze players. One of the best small museums anywhere.

places.name: Mutual Musicians Foundation
places.notes: A musicians' union hall with a late-night jam session on weekends, going until dawn.

places.name: Union Station Kansas City
places.address: 30 W Pershing Rd, Kansas City, MO 64108
places.notes: A grand 1914 station with a 95-foot ceiling, science exhibits and the free streetcar outside.

places.name: Arabia Steamboat Museum
places.notes: Cargo from an 1856 steamboat dug out of a Kansas cornfield, perfectly preserved.

places.name: Country Club Plaza
places.notes: A 1920s shopping district modeled on Seville, full of fountains. The holiday lights start on Thanksgiving.

places.name: Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts
places.notes: Two shell-shaped halls for the symphony, opera and ballet. Free tours on some days.

places.name: Harry S. Truman Library and Museum
places.notes: Truman's presidency, from the atomic bomb to the Marshall Plan. His home is nearby.

places.name: GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium
places.notes: Home of the Chiefs and the loudest crowd in football. Come early for the tailgates.

places.name: Kauffman Stadium
places.notes: The Royals' ballpark, with a fountain wall in the outfield.

places.name: Loose Park
places.notes: A big rose garden and a pond near the Plaza. Bring a picnic.

places.name: Penn Valley Park
places.address: Penn Valley Park, Kansas City, MO 64108
places.notes: Rolling lawns below the WWI memorial, with the best view of the downtown skyline.

places.name: Berkley Riverfront Park
places.notes: A riverside trail and dog park along the Missouri River, a short walk from River Market.

places.name: Swope Park
places.notes: One of the country's biggest city parks, with the zoo, trails and the Starlight Theatre.

places.name: Overland Park Arboretum and Botanical Gardens
places.notes: Woodland trails and gardens on the Kansas side. The Monet garden is lovely in summer.

places.name: Shawnee Mission Park
places.notes: A big lake with paddleboards and kayaks, and a tall observation tower.
